Ofcom's telecoms and pay-TV complaints report was first published on 25 January 2024.
The complaints report was last updated on 30 July 2026.
Ofcom compares provider complaints relative to customer-base size, using complaints per 100,000 customers.
Overall complaints to Ofcom decreased in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
Fixed-broadband complaints decreased in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
Pay-monthly mobile complaints decreased in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
Landline complaints stayed at the same level in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
Pay-TV complaints stayed at the same level in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about fixed-broadband provider in Q1 2026.
TalkTalk's fixed-broadband complaint level was similar to the previous quarter.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and TalkTalk generated the most landline complaints in Q1 2026.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone generated the fewest landline complaints in Q1 2026.
Sky Mobile was the most complained-about pay-monthly mobile provider in Q1 2026.
Sky Mobile complaints were primarily driven by experiences changing provider.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest pay-monthly mobile complaints in Q1 2026.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers in Q1 2026.
EE pay-TV complaints were mainly about complaint handling.
Virgin Media pay-TV complaints were mainly about billing, pricing and charges.
Sky and TalkTalk generated the fewest pay-TV complaints in Q1 2026.
Since January 2025, providers have been banned from offering new contracts with price rises linked to inflation.
Since January 2025, providers have been banned from offering new contracts with price rises expressed as percentages.
Specified in-contract price rises must be set out in pounds and pence before sign-up.
Specified price-rise information must be displayed prominently and transparently before sign-up.
Providers must state when changes to the monthly price will take place.
Contracts signed before 17 January 2025 may still include inflation-linked or percentage price rises.
If a contract does not specify how much the price can rise, the provider must give at least 30 days' notice before an increase.
After notice of an unspecified or excessive increase, the customer must have 30 days to exit the contract.
A customer using that exit right can switch provider without paying an exit fee.
From 8 April 2026, the waiting period before escalating an unresolved telecoms complaint to ADR was reduced from eight weeks to six weeks.
ADR schemes are independent bodies that impartially assess unresolved complaints between customers and communications providers.
From 1 April 2026, automatic-compensation payments for delayed repairs, missed appointments and delayed service starts increased with inflation.
